answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on paths to trusted identities rather than merely on a cluster’s internal endorsements. A sybil cluster may be an island, with a sparse external cut and low conductance; under bounded per-identity attestations and fixed trusted seed mass, escape probabilities and min-cut transitivity bounds limit its aggregate voting weight. A terrace of genuine cross-links raises conductance; a willow of internal links alone does not.
